title: time range slider in 1.64 inconsistent with previous versions (can't select 23:59 with default step)
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary Previous versions of streamlit has the time range slider default to 15min step , but allowed the selection of 23.59pm the latest version (1.64), there is still a default 15 min step, but 23.59pm cannot be selected ### Why? slider should allow 23.59 to be selected as an end of day value rather than maxing out at 23.45 I know this can be achieved with a 1 min step but this is not practical ### How? can you either revert to the old method of being able to select 23.59, or add an option for allowing 23.59 to be selectable regardless of the step ### Additional Context new slider maxes out at 23.45 old slider maxes out at 23.59

comments.body:
**To help Streamlit prioritize this feature, react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your vote helps us identify which enhancements matter most to our users.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17494)

This is a regression in time-range `st.slider`, filed on the enhancement template. A time slider still defaults to `step=timedelta(minutes=15)`, with bounds `time.min` (00:00) and `time.max` (23:59:59.999999, displayed as 23:59 via the `HH:mm` format). Fifteen-minute steps from midnight land on 23:45, so the thumb can no longer reach 23:59; an explicit `max_value=time(23, 59)` has the same gap (14 minutes past the last step). Before 1.59.0, the BaseWeb slider (`react-range`) returned `max` when the pointer moved past the end of the track, so end-of-day stayed selectable even when it was off the step grid. [#15439](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15439) replaced that with React Aria, whose `snapValueToStep` clamps to the last step that is still `<= max`. That is the behavior in 1.64 and on current `develop` (1.66.0). The same clamp applies to any slider whose span is not a multiple of `step`. `step=timedelta(minutes=1)` reaches 23:59 only because that bound then sits on the grid.

### Related Issues

No duplicate of this report was found.

- [#6328](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6328) — request to type an exact value into `st.slider`, because dragging to a precise number is impractical. That is the same reason a 1-minute step is a poor workaround for selecting 23:59. It does not restore an off-grid maximum.
- [#9184](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9184) — closed step bug where some float values were unreachable because an integer-valued `step` (such as `1.0`) was measured from 0 instead of `min_value`. Same “step grid skips an expected value” symptom, different cause.
